items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: I played with Bobby in Puerto Rico.

ctx.x: The country folks, they call it the bush. And you haven't seen poverty until you see it in Africa. Children with these bloated stomachs and all that -- it's pathetic. So if you hear anybody talk about refusing to give aid to Africa, they don't know what they're talking about, because they need it badly. And they're great people, you know. They're wonderful people. With all their poverty, they're as dignified as you've ever seen anything in your life. They don't bend, they don't stoop. Great people. When it comes…
Can I ask you -- the trumpet player you were speaking about that performed with Jackie Gleason, was that Bobby Hackett?
Oh, no, no. I played with Bobby in Puerto Rico. No, that wasn't Bobby.

items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: you know who came to our Hot Feet Club? Boston Blackie made at least two visits a week

ctx.x: And we were then splitting the money -- the money had to go eight -- 16 ways, and I was coming home with $10.00 and $15.00 a night, but you know who came to our Hot Feet Club? Boston Blackie made at least two visits a week -- the original Boston Blackie. He was -- had the most handsome teeth of anybody I've ever seen. And he always grinned. He'd paste $1,000.00 bills on each one of the waiter's heads and let them run around all night with $1,000.00 pasted on his
forehead, you know. He'd collect them up before he left.
